pie: Hyudʰsmṓs h₃réǵm̥ moréyont. nu tósyo suHnús h₂wékst só-kʷe Hwérdʰt. nu bʰéh₂t tósyo méh₂trey. h₁yós méne ph₂térm̥ gʷʰént tósmey kʷoynéh₂m déh₃oh₂. nu tósyo h₁éḱwoh₁ tóns wéǵʰet. nu tóy gʷm̥yóntm̥ tóm kʷḱént. nu gʷʰént tóns. nu sn̥gʷént tóy ní h₁opéyet-kʷe tóybʰos kʷoynéh₂m. nu só h₃rḗǵs bʰúHt. nu bʰúHt tósyo ḱléwos méǵh₂.
english: Warriors killed the king. His son grew up, and became strong. He spoke to his mother: "Whoever killed my father, to him I shall give punishment." He drove his two horses to them. They saw him coming. He struck them down. They fell down, and he gave them punishment. Then he became king. His fame became great.

pie: wiHrós déḱm̥t wétōs dweh₂róy h₂éǵroy wr̥ǵyét. nu h₁ést wétōs dweh₂réh₂. nu tósyo kólHonm̥ h₁r̥sḱét. nu ḱwṓ h₂én légʰyet. nu kʷéḱt ḱwṓ tóm tóm-kʷe ǵnéh₃t. nu tóm gʷm̥yét só-kʷe mért. nu sédyet tósyo pótnih₂ h₂én. nu tā́m h₁r̥sḱét. nu tóm ne ǵnéh₃t. nu só wéwket. pótnih₂ me ne ǵn̥néh₃si? ǵn̥néh₃mi te. nu tóh₁ mudtā́m.
english: For ten years the man worked in a far field. The years were long. Then he came to his own hill. A dog was lying there. The dog saw him, and knew him. It came to him, and died. His wife was sitting there. He came to her. She did not know him. He said: "Wife, do you not know me?" "I know you." The two became glad.

pie: deywṓs péruni sdént. nu wérh₁yet dyḗws ph₂tḗr. kʷís mórtons h₂léksēti? nu h₂éwsōs sékʷt. tóns h₂léksōh₂. nu dʰéǵʰōm mléwHt. tóns upó h₂léksōh₂. nu h₁n̥gʷnís bʰéh₂t. tóns h₂éǵroy h₂léksōh₂. wékʷos wos h₁wésu h₁ésti. nu h₂wéyst dʰéǵʰōm méh₂tēr tóns séh₂-kʷe méwdt. nu tóy swéh₂du wódr̥ ph₃ént.
english: The gods sat down on the mountain. Father Sky spoke: "Who will protect the mortals?" Dawn said: "I shall protect them." The earth said: "I shall protect them from below." Fire said: "I shall protect them in the field." "Good is your word." Mother Earth heard them, and she became glad. They drank sweet water.

pie: wiHrṓs wiHróm logʰéyont. nu tóm ph₂wénh₁ h₁éwsont. nu h₁ést péh₂wr̥ h₁rowdʰóm. nu sth₂éh₁yet tósyo ph₂tḗr ph₂wéni. nu tósyo pótnih₂ péh₂wr̥ spéḱyet. nu só tóybʰos wéwket. tósmey ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ dʰh₁té. nu dʰh₁ént tósmey ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥. nu só tóybʰos déḱm̥t gʷṓs dédeh₃t. h₁ésti ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos tósmey. nu gʷh₂tós tóm h₁épt tósyo-kʷe ḱléwos ne néḱt.
english: Men laid the hero down. They burned him with fire. The fire was red. His father stood by the fire. His wife looked at the fire. He said to them: "Set a famous name for him!" They set a famous name for him. Then he gave them ten cattle. Imperishable fame is his. Death took him, and his fame did not vanish.

pie: sh₂wéns dʰugh₂tḗr h₂ékʷeh₂m gʷéh₂t. h₁ést h₂ékʷeh₂ méǵh₂ih₂ tósyeh₂i-kʷe ní séngʷt. séh₂ bʰéyh₂t séh₂-kʷe h₂éǵt. diwés me suHnúh₁ ḱlutóm. h₂ékʷeh₂s me spr̥tóm. h₂wistā́m tóh₁ tā́m. nu h₁ludʰétām kʷékʷloy wéǵʰetām-kʷe dwóh₁ HéHḱuh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁ tóm. nu tā́m h₂ékʷeh₂s duktā́m tā́m-kʷe kʷékʷloy sodéyetām. nu wédʰetām tā́m sóh₂wl̥. tód méwdt tód-kʷe wéwket. méne dʰugh₂térm̥ spr̥tóm. wiHróns h₂léksetom.
english: The daughter of the Sun went to the water. The water was great, and she sank down in it. She became afraid, and she said: "Hear me, O two sons of Sky! Free me from the water!" They heard her. They arrived on a chariot, and two swift horses carried it. They drew her out of the water and set her on the chariot. Then they led her to the Sun. He became glad, and he said: "You have freed my daughter! Protect men!"

pie: méǵh₂ih₂ h₁ógʷʰis péruni ḱéyto ḱélet-kʷe déh₂nuh₂ h₁n̥dóm. dʰéǵʰōm gʷówes-kʷe tr̥syónt. nu deywṓs wiHrṓy wr̥h₁ént. h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰn̥dʰí. tóns spr̥dʰí. nu tósyo ǵʰoysóm sléh₂gʷt pró-kʷe h₁éyt. widét h₁ógʷʰis gʷm̥sḱóntm̥ tóm. nu gʷʰént h₁ógʷʰim. pérwr̥ wí bʰéydt. nu déh₂nuh₂ mélh₃t péh₃t-kʷe dʰéǵʰōm wódr̥. nu dh₃ént deywṓs tósmey ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos.
english: The great serpent lay on the mountain, and it was hiding the rivers inside. The earth was thirsty and the cattle were thirsty. Then the gods spoke to the hero: "Slay the serpent! Free them!" He took his spear and went forward. The serpent saw him coming. He slew the serpent. He split the mountain apart. The rivers came forth, and the earth drank the water. The gods gave imperishable fame to him.

pie: Hyudʰsmṓs h₃rḗǵnih₂m̥ lm̥bʰént tā́m-kʷe gʷṓs-kʷe h₂epó h₁élh₂t. nu h₃rḗǵn̥yeh₂s bʰréh₂tēr wiHrṓy wéwket. tā́m spr̥dʰí. méǵh₂m̥ toy misdʰh₁óm déh₃oh₂. nu tóns séh₂gyet. nu pérwr̥ h₁ért widéh₁yet-kʷe sédyontn̥s tóns. nu moréyet tóns. nu kʷéḱt h₃rḗǵnih₂ tóm só-kʷe tā́m spért. nu ǵʰéyt tóns h₂epó tā́m-kʷe tósyeh₂s bʰréh₂term̥ wédʰet h₁yós tósmey misdʰh₁óm dédeh₃t. nu ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos tóm gʷéh₂t.
english: Warriors seized the queen, and drove her and the cattle away. The brother of the queen said to the hero: "Free her! I shall give you a great prize." He tracked them. He arrived at the mountain, and saw them sitting. He killed them. The queen saw him, and he freed her. He drove them away, and led her to her brother, who gave him the prize. Imperishable fame went to him.

pie: wĺ̥kʷos h₁éḱwom kʷéḱt. nu wĺ̥kʷos sékʷt. h₁éḱwe twé gʷr̥h₃ṓh₂. nu h₁éḱwos mléwHt. wĺ̥kʷe méne tpḗrsneh₂m spéḱye. nu h₁mé gʷr̥h₃é. nu wĺ̥kʷos h₂énti h₁r̥sḱét h₁éḱwosyo-kʷe tpḗrsneh₂m spéḱyet. nu stunédt h₁éḱwos wĺ̥kʷom tpḗrsneh₂h₁. nu wĺ̥kʷos ní séngʷt só-kʷe wéwket. h₁éḱwosyo wékʷōs swéh₂duh₂ h₁ést h₁éḱwosyo-kʷe tpḗrsneh₂ h₁mé stunédt. h₁yós swéh₂duh₂ wékʷōs bʰebʰóydʰe mértis tóm widét.
english: A wolf saw a horse. The wolf said: "I shall devour you, horse." The horse said: "Look at my heel, wolf! Then devour me!" The wolf came near, and looked at the heel of the horse. The horse struck the wolf with the heel. The wolf fell down, and said: "Sweet were the words of the horse, and the heel of the horse struck me." Whoever trusts sweet words, death finds him.

pie: sóh₂wl̥ wiHrṓy tósyo dʰugh₂térm̥ déh₃t tósmey-kʷe déḱm̥t gʷṓs h₁opéyet. nu só sh₂wéns ǵm̥rós bʰúHt. wédʰet dwóh₁ HéHḱuh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁. nu tóh₁ kʷékʷlom wéǵʰetām sédt-kʷe séh₂ tósmi. nu kʷéḱt tósyo méh₂tēr tā́m. nu méh₂tēr sékʷt. dʰúgh₂ter moy priHéh₂ h₁sdʰí. suHnóws moy pótnih₂ h₁sdʰí. pótnih₂ h₁ésoh₂. nu deywṓs tóh₁ h₂léksoyh₁ent tóh₁-kʷe gʷíh₃woyh₁tām.
english: The Sun gave his daughter to the hero, and gave him ten cattle. Now he became the son-in-law of the Sun. He led two swift horses. They carried the chariot, and she sat on it. His mother saw her. The mother said: "O daughter, be dear to me! Be the wife of my son!" "I shall be a wife." May the gods protect the two, and may the two live!

pie: h₃rḗḱs súHnum wl̥nh₁to.
english: The king wanted a son.

pie: owis eḱwōskʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses

pie: h₁ógʷʰis kl̥Héni ḱéyto gʷr̥h₃ét-kʷe h₃rḗǵn̥yeh₂s gʷṓs. nu sékʷt h₃rḗǵnih₂ Hyudʰsmóybʰos. kʷís h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰéneti? nu tóy bʰih₂ént. nu wiHrós úd stéh₂t só-kʷe wérh₁yet. h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰénoh₂. h₁yód h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰénesi méne toy dʰugh₂térm̥ déh₃oh₂. nu só pró h₁éyt. nu widéh₁yet h₁ógʷʰis gʷm̥sḱóntm̥ tóm. nu gʷʰént h₁ógʷʰim. nu h₃rḗǵnih₂ tósmey tósyeh₂s dʰugh₂térm̥ h₁opéyet. nu gʷéh₂t méǵh₂ ḱléwos tóm.
english: A serpent lay on the hill, and it devoured the cattle of the queen. The queen said to the warriors: "Who will slay the serpent?" They became afraid. A man stood up and said: "I shall slay the serpent." "If you slay the serpent, I shall give you my daughter." He went forward. The serpent saw him coming. He slew the serpent. The queen gave him her daughter. Great fame went to him.

pie: wiHrós h₂élyos-kʷe h₂éǵrom h₁ludʰétām. h₂énti sth₂éh₁yetām. nu h₂élyos wéwket. kʷís h₁ési? h₃rēǵés suHnús h₁ésmi. h₁yós dedwóye só h₂epó léyttu. nu séh₁t h₂élyos tósyo ǵʰoysóm ǵʰoysós-kʷe tóm dʰégʷʰh₂t. nu léh₁t só tósyo gʷéru térdt-kʷe gʷéru h₂élyosyo ḱérd. nu só ní séngʷt só-kʷe mért. nu só h₂élyosyo h₁éḱwoh₁ lémbʰt ǵʰéyt-kʷe tóh₁ h₂epó. nu ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos tósmey bʰwéh₂t.
english: The hero and the other man arrived at the field. They stood opposite one another. The other man said: "Who are you?" "I am the son of the king. Whoever is afraid, let him go away!" The other man let go his spear, and the spear passed by him. Then he let go his spear, and the spear bored through the heart of the other man. He fell down, and died. He took the two horses of the other man and drove them away. Imperishable fame arose for him.

pie: ph₂tḗr tósyo suHnówey wérh₁t. méne wékʷōs ḱludʰí. gʷṓs h₂ówins-kʷe ph₂sdʰí. h₂élyosyo gʷṓs mē stéh₂yes. h₁yós ḱléwos h₂isḱḗti só h₁wésus h₁sdʰí. gʷémt mértis wiHróns. méne súHnu mē bʰéyh₂s. nu ḱléwt só téh₂ só-kʷe mléwHt. tód dʰéh₁oh₂. nu só méǵh₂s bʰúHt bʰúHt-kʷe tósyo h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm.
english: The father spoke to his son: "Hear my words. Guard the cattle and the sheep. Do not steal the cattle of another. Whoever seeks fame, let him be good. Death comes to men. Do not become afraid, my son!" He heard them, and said: "I shall do so." He became great, and his name became famous.

pie: deywṓm gʷówes kl̥Héni h₁sént. h₁yód h₂én h₁regʷesyét h₂éngʷʰis gʷṓs stéh₂yet tóns-kʷe pérwr̥ h₁n̥dó h₁élh₂t. h₁yód h₂éwsōs h₂wést tóy gʷṓs h₂isḱónt. nu deywós sékʷt. gʷówes nos lelikʷḗr. kʷís tóns stéh₂yet? nu wiHrós mléwHt. h₂éngʷʰis tóns stéh₂yet. gʷṓs séh₂gyōh₂. nu pérwr̥ h₁ért tód-kʷe skélHt. nu h₂éngʷʰis bʰéyh₂t. nu só h₂éngʷʰim moréyet. nu gʷówes h₁n̥dʰént. dyḗws ph₂tḗr h₁uséwōm déh₃tōr gʷṓs ph₂syéh₁t.
english: The cattle of the gods were on the hill. When it was getting dark there, a snake stole the cattle and drove them into the mountain. When Dawn became bright, they sought the cattle. A god said: "Our cattle are gone! Who stole them?" Then a man said: "A snake stole them. I shall seek out the cattle." He arrived at the mountain, and split it open. The snake became afraid. Then he killed the snake. The cattle came forth. May Father Sky, giver of good things, guard the cattle!

pie: mórtos ǵʰémi légʰt. nu h₁ludʰét mértis tóm só-kʷe mért. nu tósyo bʰréh₂tēr légʰyontm̥ tóm widét só-kʷe bʰéyh₂t. nu deywóybʰos wérh₁t. só ḱéytor ne-kʷe me dedórḱe. nu tóy h₂ǵént. mórtōs mr̥wé. mértis wiHróns gʷémt. h₁wésu ḱléwos ne néḱt. nu dʰh₁ént tóy tósmey ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥. nu tósyo h₁nómn̥ méǵh₂ bʰúHt.
english: A mortal lay down on the earth. Death arrived at his side, and he died. His brother saw him lying down, and he became afraid. He said to the gods: "He is lying flat, and he does not see me." They said: "Mortals die. Death comes to men. Good fame does not vanish." They set a famous name for him. Then his name became great.

pie: h₃rēǵés bʰréh₂tēr suHnúh₁ h₁épt logʰéyet-kʷe tóh₁ ǵʰémi. nu só léytt. nu ḱléwt wl̥kʷíh₂s tóh₁ tóh₁ gʷm̥yét tóh₁-kʷe h₂élet. nu poh₂imḗn tóh₁ kʷéḱt. nu tóh₁ h₂ukstā́m tóh₁-kʷe Hwr̥dʰtā́m. nu poh₂imnéy bʰh₂tā́m. kʷís nos ph₂tḗr h₁ésti? nu só h₂éǵt. h₃rḗǵs wos ph₂tḗr h₁ésti. tósyo bʰréh₂tēr woh₃ lémbʰt. nu tóm gʷh₂tā́m tóm-kʷe moréyetām. nu tóh₁ ḱlutóh₁ bʰúHtām.
english: The brother of the king seized the two sons, and laid them down on the earth. Then he went away. A she-wolf heard them, came to them, and nourished them. A shepherd saw them. The two grew up and became strong. They spoke to the shepherd: "Who is our father?" He said: "The king is your father. His brother seized you." The two went to him and killed him. The two became famous.

pie: h₁n̥gʷnís deywóybʰos léytt séngʷt-kʷe h₂ékʷās ní. tóy tóm h₂isḱónt. h₁n̥gʷnís kúdʰe h₁ésti? nu h₁n̥gʷnís h₁rowdʰós h₁ést. nu kʷéḱt skʷálos tóm wédney só-kʷe bʰéh₂t. só h₂ékʷeh₂su h₁ésti. nu tóy h₂ékʷās h₁r̥sḱónt tóy-kʷe skʷént. h₁ń̥gʷni h₁n̥dʰdʰí. ḱlutóm toy h₁nómn̥ dʰéh₁omes. nu h₁nédʰt h₁n̥gʷnís wédn̥s. nu h₁pént tóy tóm tóm-kʷe mórtons wédʰont. nu mórtōs ph₂wénh₁ pékʷonti. h₁ń̥gʷni nos h₁uséwōm déh₃tor h₂lékse.
english: Fire went away from the gods, and sank down into the waters. They were seeking him. "Where is Fire?" Fire was red. A large fish saw him in the water and spoke: "He is in the waters." They went to the waters, and they said: "O Fire, come forth! We shall set a famous name for you." Fire came forth from the water. They seized him and led him to the mortals. Now mortals cook with fire. O Fire, giver of good things, protect us!

pie: wiHrós tósyo bʰréh₂tēr-kʷe kéh₃tum kʷékʷloy gʷh₂tā́m. nu tósyo bʰréh₂tēr HéHḱuh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁ h₂éǵet. nu Hyudʰsmóns h₁ludʰétām. nu stunédt só tóns. nu séh₁t h₂élyos tósyo ǵʰoysóm ǵʰoysós-kʷe bʰréh₂tr̥s ḱérd térdt. nu só kʷékʷlōd ní séngʷt. nu sléh₂gʷt só tóh₁ tóh₁-kʷe pró ǵʰéyt. nu bʰéret tóm kh₃téws. nu só sékʷt. méne bʰréh₂ter lelóykʷth₂e. ḱléwos toy ne néḱeti.
english: The hero and his brother went to the fight on a chariot. His brother drove the two swift horses. They arrived at the warriors. He struck them. Another man let go his spear, and the spear bored through the heart of the brother. He fell down from the chariot. Then he seized them, and drove them forward. Then he carried him away from the fight. He said: "My brother, you are gone! Your fame will not vanish."

pie: pótnih₂ kl̥Héni sédyet. nu stóygʰom spéḱyet. nu wétōs h₁éyt. nu trémt tósyeh₂s ḱḗr. nu séh₂ bʰéh₂t. h₂éwsos méne wiHróm wédʰe. h₂éǵrons h₂ékʷās-kʷe dedórḱth₂e. tóm dedórḱth₂e? tóm dedórḱh₂e. stóygʰoy gʷm̥sḱétes. nu pótnih₂ gʷm̥sḱóntm̥ tóm kʷéḱt. nu tóm ǵnéh₃t tósyeh₂s-kʷe ḱḗr méwdt. nu h₁r̥sḱét só tā́m. nu tóh₁ mudtā́m.
english: The wife was sitting on the hill. She was looking at the path. The years went by. Her heart trembled. She spoke: "O Dawn, bring my husband! You see the fields and the waters. Do you see him?" "I see him. He is coming along the path." The wife saw him coming. She knew him, and her heart became glad. He reached her. The two became glad.

pie: wiHrós tósyo h₁éḱwoh₁ kéh₃tum h₂éǵet. nu sth₂éh₁yet sewyós h₁éḱwos. nu só tósmey bʰéh₂t. kh₃téws te bʰérōmes. mértis te h₂énti h₁ésti. h₁éḱwe tód wóydh₂e. mértis me h₂énti h₁ésti. HéHḱuh₁ me h₁éḱwoh₁ kéh₃tum bʰéretom. nu h₁éḱwoh₁ tóm kéh₃tum bʰéretām. nu térdt ǵʰoysós tósyo ḱérd kʷékʷlōd-kʷe séngʷt. nu gʷéh₂t ń̥dʰgʷʰitom ḱléwos tóm.
english: The hero drove his two horses to the fight. The left horse stood. It spoke to him: "We shall carry you away from the fight. Death is near you." "I know it, horse. Death is near me. Carry me to the fight, swift horses!" The two horses carried him to the fight. Then a spear bored through his heart, and he fell from the chariot. Imperishable fame went to him.

pie: dyḗws ǵʰémi ḱéyto. tḱyént wiHrṓs h₁entér h₂én-kʷe h₁regʷesyét. wiHrós Hwérdʰt. nu úd stéh₂t tóh₁-kʷe wí stunédt. dyḗws upér h₁ést h₁ést-kʷe dʰéǵʰōm Hn̥dʰí. nu upér léwkt tóy-kʷe péri spéḱyont. dyéw nos ph₂tér dʰéǵʰom méh₂ter ḱlutóm. ḱlutā́m tóh₁ n̥smé.
english: Sky lay on Earth. Men lived in between, and it was getting dark there. A man became strong. He stood up, and pushed them apart. Sky was above, and Earth was below. Then it became bright above, and they looked around. "Father Sky, Mother Earth, hear us!" They heard us.

pie: h₁yód kl̥Héni h₁regʷesyét Hyudʰsmṓs ǵʰémi l̥gʰént. nu wiHrós bʰéwdʰet. nu wĺ̥kʷons h₂wéyst wĺ̥kʷōs-kʷe pró gʷm̥yónt. nu tóybʰos bʰéh₂t. Hyudʰsmṓs bʰudʰté. ǵʰoysóns wos lm̥bʰté. nu tóy bʰudʰént. nu lémbʰt wĺ̥kʷos h₂ówim. nu wĺ̥kʷons moréyont. nu wl̥kʷíh₂s léytt. nu upér léwkt. nu spéḱyet só péri. h₂óweyes gʷíh₃wont.
english: When it was getting dark on the hill, the warriors lay down on the earth. The hero was awake. He heard the wolves, and the wolves came forward. He spoke to them: "Wake up, warriors! Seize your spears!" They woke up. A wolf seized a sheep. They killed the wolves. The she-wolf went away. It became bright above. He looked around. The sheep were alive.

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

english: In winter a snake lay down. The snake became cold. A shepherd saw the snake, and seized it. He warmed it with fire. The snake became warm. Then the snake seized him. He said: "I warmed you with fire, and do you seize me?" "I am a snake." Then it killed him. Do not warm a snake! Whoever warms a snake, the snake will kill him.

pie: h₁rowdʰóns gʷṓs h₂éǵontih₂ h₂éwsōs péruns gʷm̥sḱéti. mórtōs bʰudʰént. nu ḱwónes tā́m ḱléwsonti litént-kʷe wĺ̥kʷōs h₂epó. nu wédʰeti poh₂imḗn tósyo h₂ówins pró. nu tóy wódr̥ píph₃onti. nu séh₂ tóybʰos h₁wésuh₂ dédeh₃ti. tósyeh₂s stóygʰos mréǵʰus h₁ésti. nu spéḱyeti sóh₂wl̥ tā́m séh₂-kʷe linékʷti. h₂éwsos nos diwés dʰúgh₂ter h₁rowdʰóns gʷṓs h₂éǵe. h₂wisdʰí nos.
english: Dawn, driving the red cattle, comes from the mountain. The mortals wake up. The dogs listen to her, and the wolves go away. The shepherd leads his sheep forward. They drink the water. She gives them good things. Short is her path. The Sun looks at her, and she leaves. "O Dawn, daughter of Sky, drive the red cattle to us! Hear us!"

pie: mórtos mért. nu stóygʰoy h₁éyt déh₂nu-kʷe h₁r̥té. nu légʰyetām dwóh₁ ḱwónh₁ kʷetwr̥bʰí h₃kʷbʰís h₂én. nu widétām tóh₁ tóm só-kʷe wérh₁yet. ḱwónh₁ h₁mé l̥h₁tóm. nu tóh₁ tósyo h₁nómn̥ ḱlutā́m. nu tóh₁ tóm l̥h₁tā́m. nu gʷéh₂t tód pér deywóns-kʷe h₁ludʰét. nu tóy tósmey h₁wésuh₂ dédh₃n̥t.
english: A mortal died. He went along the path, and arrived at the river. Two dogs with four eyes were lying there. They saw him, and he said: "O dogs, let me go!" They heard his name. They let him go. He went through the river, and came to the gods. They gave him good things.

pie: wiHrós Hyudʰsmós-kʷe h₂énti sth₂éh₁yetām. nu Hyudʰsmós mléwHt. wĺ̥kʷos h₁ési. gʷṓs stéh₂yesi. ḱḗr toy h₂éwis ḱḗr h₁ésti. wékʷōs toy swéh₂duh₂ h₁ésti gʷéru-kʷe toy mréǵʰu h₁ésti. méne gʷéru dweh₂róm h₁ésti. nu só mléwHt. déh₂nu pér gʷm̥yé. nu h₁r̥sḱét mórtos h₁entér. nu só bʰéh₂t. tósmōd h₂epó littóm. nu tóh₁ littā́m.
english: The hero and the warrior stood opposite one another. The warrior said: "You are a wolf. You steal cattle. Your heart is the heart of a sheep!" "Your words are sweet, and your spear is short. My spear is long." The warrior said: "Come through the river!" Then a mortal came between them. He spoke: "Go away from it, both of you!" Then the two went away.
